history_timeline.title: Binalatongan
history_timeline.description: The settlement began as Binalatongan, a riverside trading center (barter system) visited by Chinese, Japanese, and Indian traders; the name comes from balatong, the Pangasinan word for mung bean, which was abundant in the area. The Province of Pangasinan describes it as a capital of Caboloan.

history_timeline.title: Early founding (Wikipedia date)
history_timeline.description: Wikipedia's infobox dates the founding to 1578. See the 1587 entry for the documented source conflict.
history_timeline.footnote: Founding year conflict: Wikipedia says 1578; the LGU's archived history says 1587. Both lack a fully citable primary source.

history_timeline.title: Founding by Augustinian friar (LGU date)
history_timeline.description: The LGU's archived history records the community's founding by Fr. Francisco dela Lama, an Augustinian friar, in 1587.

history_timeline.title: Binalatongan becomes a vicariate
history_timeline.description: Padre Bernardo Navarro de Santa Catalina, O.P. became the first Vicar, with Fr. Juan de Castro, Fr. Marcos de San Antonio, and Bro. Juan Deza as assistants.

history_timeline.title: Malong revolt
history_timeline.description: Andres Malong led a major revolt against Spanish colonial rule; he is regarded as a native hero of Binalatongan.

history_timeline.title: Poblacion relocated across the San Juan River
history_timeline.description: After a minor uprising led by Juan Caragay in which the church and convent were set on fire, the Poblacion was relocated east of the San Juan River on November 4, 1718 (feast of St. Charles Borromeo), and the settlement was renamed San Carlos Binalatongan.

history_timeline.title: Palaris revolt
history_timeline.description: Juan dela Cruz Palaris (Pantaleon Perez) led a revolt against tribute and forced labor; his rebels held an independent government based in Binalatongan for about two years.

history_timeline.title: Renamed San Carlos by order of King Carlos III
history_timeline.description: After the revolts were defeated, King Carlos III of Spain ordered the town razed and renamed it San Carlos in his honor; the site was moved to its present location.

history_timeline.title: Cityhood under RA 4487
history_timeline.description: Republic Act No. 4487, signed June 19, 1965, converted the municipality into the City of San Carlos (the smaller zone became the Municipality of Basista under RA 4866). Cityhood took effect January 1, 1966 after local ratification.

history_timeline.title: NHCP historical marker
history_timeline.description: The National Historical Commission of the Philippines installed the "Lungsod ng San Carlos" historical marker at the city plaza.

history_timeline.title: Mango-Bamboo Festival launched
history_timeline.description: The city's signature festival promoting its mango and bamboo industries was launched; it is held in the last week of April.

history_timeline.title: World's largest mango pie
history_timeline.description: On April 26, 2011, city residents and the bakers' association baked the world's largest mango pie (100 m2, 2 inches thick) for the Mango-Bamboo Festival, using 2,000 kg of mangoes at a total cost of about P400,000.

basilica.name: Minor Basilica of Saint Dominic
basilica.description: The parish church of St. Dominic de Guzman is the city's most significant religious heritage landmark. Its current site is the third location of the church.
basilica.built_1773: A church was completed in 1773 but was destroyed by earthquakes several times.
basilica.rebuilt_1803: Rebuilt in 1803, it measured 89 yards long and 22 yards wide (per old LGU text).
basilica.minor_basilica: Declared a Minor Basilica by Pope Francis on July 6, 2022, and solemnly proclaimed on January 14, 2023.
basilica.dominican_presence: Traces to 1587 in Binalatongan; the town's first church tradition dates from the late 16th century.

landmarks.name: Speaker Eugenio P. Perez Sr. Memorial Building
landmarks.description: Named for the late Speaker; serves as the city museum (the NHCP 1988 marker is installed at the plaza).

landmarks.name: San Carlos City Plaza (City Park), Palaris Street
landmarks.description: Public plaza used for festivals and public viewing; described as a heritage park.

landmarks.name: Quadricentennial Arch (Bolingit)
landmarks.description: Commemorative arch cited among the city's interesting spots.

landmarks.name: Binalatongan Ruins (San Juan)
landmarks.description: Ruins relating to the city's pre-San-Carlos history as Binalatongan.

landmarks.name: San Carlos City Hall (Palaris Street)
landmarks.description: Government heritage structure featured in city images.

landmarks.name: Ancestral houses
landmarks.description: Noted as a feature of the old city.

heritage.legend: The sunken church bell of the San Juan River: the great bell of the Binalatongan belfry - said to be the biggest and most sonorous in the province - was lost when the raft carrying it across the river collapsed; local legend says a mermaid guards it at the bottom of the river.
